text:
morgan: FYI master is red after the dependency merge that landed this morning, looks like the manylinux matrix job is failing across a few runners

jules: pinged for rerun? I can kick off a rebuild but want a quick triage first to avoid wasting cycles :slightly_smiling_face:

ci-bot: build #8152 — https://ci.internal/redwood/8152 — FAILED (linux-manylinux-x86_64 / py310)

sam: I glanced at the logs, failing at wheel install for cryptography 40.0.0 wheel tag mismatch on manylinux2014. Could be the new binary wheel or the pip resolver picking a different build on that image

alex: repro locally in a docker manylinux2014 image: pip install -r requirements.txt errors out with 
```
ERROR: cryptography-40.0.0-cp310-cp310-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl is not a supported wheel on this platform
```
I also saw a warning about a transitive cffi bump in the resolver output

morgan: the merge included the new constraints file from infra/dep-updates and bumped cryptography via a transitive pin. Someone added a relaxed platform tag override in the pip config earlier this week — could be interacting badly

jules: can you paste the pip debug output? `pip debug --verbose` or `pip install -vvv cryptography==40.0.0` helps show what wheel tags are considered

alex: pasted minimal repro here: 
```
$ docker run --rm -it quay.io/pypa/manylinux2014_x86_64 /bin/bash -c \"python -m pip install cryptography==40.0.0 -vvv\"
Collecting cryptography==40.0.0
  Using cached cryptography-40.0.0-cp310-cp310-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl (4.1 MB)
  ERROR: cryptography-40.0.0-cp310-cp310-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl is not a supported wheel on this platform

platform tags: cp310-cp310-manylinux2014_x86_64 vs expected cp310-cp310-musllinux_*
```

sam: interesting — our CI manylinux image seems to have glibc mismatch or the runner is actually using a musl-based container for speed. Did the matrix job change the image recently?

carol: I didn't touch the image. @infra-release, any recent changes to the matrix job images?

morgan: merge-bot changed the job definition to use the `fast-builder` pool to speed things up (PR #4123). That pool is backed by an Alpine-musl based image for other builds. Oops. That explains the musl vs manylinux conflict

jules: plan: revert pool change for the manylinux matrix job, add an explicit `manylinux2014` runner label, and rerun CI. Meanwhile we should add a guard in the job config: assert image matches expected glibc tag.

sam: I can open a tiny PR to pin the runner label and add a quick check in the job script: `if [ \"$(uname -s)\" != \"Linux\" ] || [ ! -f /usr/glibc-version ]; then echo \"wrong base image\"; exit 1; fi`

alex: LGTM. Also we should add a note in the dep-updates checklist: "do not change runner pool for manylinux jobs"

ci-bot: retrigger requested by jules — queued rebuild for #8152 (will run after pool rollback)

morgan: thanks. marking this as triaged — followup: revert pool change, rerun CI, and consider pinning cryptography to the wheel compatible build until infra images are normalized. :white_check_mark:
